subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw make per-agent workspace confinement a default security boundary, or keep host-wide file access as a trusted-operator default with opt-in `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` and sandboxing?
rationale: Current docs and tests intentionally preserve host-wide access by default, while VISION.md prioritizes security and safe defaults; changing that boundary affects compatibility, security posture, and operator workflows.

options.title: Define default confinement policy
options.body: Choose the default boundary and upgrade path before merging subset fixes, then require implementation and docs to match that policy.

options.title: Keep opt-in confinement
options.body: Leave host-wide file tools as the trusted-operator default and close or narrow this issue only after documenting the recommended `tools.fs.workspaceOnly`/sandbox/policy workflow.

options.title: Land a partial hardening first
options.body: Adopt a narrow PR such as relative traversal containment while explicitly tracking the broader default-boundary decision separately.

recommendation.title: Define default confinement policy
recommendation.body: Choose the default boundary and upgrade path before merging subset fixes, then require implementation and docs to match that policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The earlier optional guard and recent current-main merge history both route this boundary decision to Peter, with secops/codeowner review needed for any implementation.
